newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end higher in thinner volume.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end higher in thinner volume.

text.p: Brazilian stocks continued slightly higher Thursday, closing up 0.19 percent in thinner volume after Wall Street closed with a record high ahead of the July 4 Independence Day holiday, brokers said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 48 most active shares rose 25 points to 13,285 points at the close. Market turnover was 922 million reais ($861.7 million).
"The market opened strong and saw some profit-taking, but it managed to close slightly higher on the back of Wall Street's strong performance," a broker said.
The release of U.S. job figures caused a surge of 100 points in the Dow Jones index to 7,895.91 points, as Wall Street closed down early for the Independence Day holiday.
Brokers said Wall Streets early close brought down volume in the Brazilian market as foreign investors scaled down their activities.
Blue-chips remained more or less stable with most posting slight gains like Telebras prefered.
Telebras prefered closed up 0.17 points at 174 reais after January to May results came in as expected.
State oil firm Petrobras prefered fell 2.88 percent to 303 reais and federal power holding Eletrobras prefered rose 2.26 percent to 680 reais.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
